model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Recorded as the evaluating session's actual runtime identity (Opus 5, 1M context; exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]), not the evaluator value pinned in the agent definition. Scores are comparable only to other rubric10-semantic scores produced by this same evaluator.

applicability_resolution.note: All five trigger conditions resolved before scoring. Element 4 is gated per sub-element, not as a whole: sub-elements 1-2 carry the governance disjunct, sub-elements 3-5 do not.

conditions.basis: E1 description and keywords name only immortalized and donor-derived cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSC and its NPC/neuron/cardiomyocyte derivatives); no participant, patient, or clinical-research terms. E8 collection_mechanisms describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, ICC-IF confocal microscopy and CRISPRi lentiviral screens, with no human participant recruitment. direct_collection.is_direct is false with the explanation that data came from commercially available cell lines rather than from individuals.

E2 ip_restrictions states that 'a Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use', and that commercial use requires separate license negotiation with UCSD, Stanford and/or UCSF. That is an E2 field stating a governance constraint that applies, so it is non-circular with respect to Element 4's own fields. The regulatory_restrictions block on its own is a record that no restriction applies (FDA Regulated: No; no export control stated) and is NOT counted as a constraint per #1060, and confidentiality_level is absent; the applicable constraint comes from ip_restrictions. The dataset also derives from donor material (KOLF2.1J from a healthy male Northern European donor via HipSci), the case the sub-element 1-2 rationale names explicitly.

conditions.condition: Datasets shared and available for reuse
conditions.basis: distribution_formats populated (format ZIP, media_type application/zip, access_urls on the UVA Dataverse Data Access API); publisher https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/ with a resolvable release DOI; ten file_collections with per-file MD5 checksums and sizes; license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 explicitly permits share and adapt.

conditions.condition: Software tools produced as dataset output
conditions.basis: E10 external_resources references code repositories: the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, the FAIRSCAPE framework at https://fairscape.github.io under the MIT License, and the Integrative Modeling Platform at http://integrativemodeling.org. E8's own fields were not used as the signal.

conditions.condition: Data collection identified AND datasets shared
conditions.basis: acquisition_methods (3 entries) and collection_mechanisms (4 entries) are populated with instrument-level detail, and the shared condition above is met.

citation carries a full Dataverse citation string, and related_datasets names the CM4AI preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 as is_described_by plus two further publications; the shared condition is met.

issues_detected.description: The only access URL given is a truncated Dataverse Data Access API base path, 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/', with no datafile identifier appended. As written it does not resolve to any file, so it is a pattern rather than a usable download link. The ten file_collections carry MD5 checksums and names but no per-file persistent identifiers or URLs.
issues_detected.recommendation: Append the Dataverse datafile ids (or the per-file persistent ids) so each file_collection resolves, or replace the bare API base with the release landing page URL on dataverse.lib.virginia.edu.

issues_detected.description: Only the archive container is declared as the distribution format. format is ZIP and media_type is application/zip, with no statement of the interior data formats for the four modalities: no image format for the immunofluorescence archives, no mass-spectrometry format for the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, and no matrix or count format for the perturb-seq atlas. No character encoding is given. A reuser cannot determine what software will read the contents.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the interior formats per file collection (for example TIFF or PNG for imaging, mzML or MaxQuant tables for mass spectrometry, MTX or h5ad for single-cell) and the text encoding for any tabular members.

issues_detected.description: Five file_collections are typed collection_type: processed_data, yet no processing is documented anywhere in the record. preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent. The MuSIC pipeline described in notes produces the computed cell maps that the record itself states are NOT in this release, so it does not account for how the released processed files were derived from the raw acquisitions.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the processing that turned the raw acquisitions into the processed_data archives (peptide and protein identification and quantification for the mass-spectrometry files, guide assignment and count-matrix construction for perturb-seq), or record explicitly that the release page does not describe it.

issues_detected.description: Version ordering is not monotonic across the release chain. This June 2026 release is recorded as version 2.0, while version_access records the earlier June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) and October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) both as Version 2.1, and the March 2025 release as Version 1.4. A later release carrying a lower version number than two of its predecessors is not flagged in source_caveats, unlike the other date anomalies the record does flag.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note in source_caveats that the Dataverse version numbering is per-dataset rather than per-collection, or reconcile the recorded version values against the release pages.

issues_detected.description: The conforms_to claim of RO-Crate packaging is explicitly attributed to the preprint and the March 2025 and June 2025 releases, not to the June 2026 release being documented; the record states the June 2026 file listing names only cm4ai_release_metadata.zip without stating its internal format. The structured conforms_to_standard value RO_CRATE asserts the claim without carrying that qualification, so the prose caveat and the enum value disagree in confidence.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either verify the packaging format of cm4ai_release_metadata.zip for this release or mark the conforms_to_standard value as inherited from prior releases.

issues_detected.description: raw_data_sources marks the perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and in MDA-MB-468 cells as Embargoed, and known_limitations repeats that among the external data links, yet the release itself distributes cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip with MD5 checksums and publication dates. The embargo evidently applies to the external repository deposits rather than to the Dataverse files, but the record does not say so, leaving the two statements apparently in conflict.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that the embargo applies to the external repository deposits, and name which subsets are unavailable in the Dataverse release itself, if any.

issues_detected.description: The software_and_tools slot is empty while seven tools and frameworks with repository and documentation URLs are carried in external_resources and a pipeline description sits in the free-text notes. The content is present and actionable but is not in the slot a consumer would query, and no versions are given for any tool.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate software_and_tools with the Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE, MuSIC, NDEx and IMP entries, each with its repository URL and, where the sources state one, its version.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided. The variables slot is absent and no data dictionary is given for the tabular members of the release, notably the SEC-MS elution profiles and the perturb-seq cell atlas. The instance-level ontology CURIEs on data_substrate and data_topic characterise modality rather than columns, so they do not substitute for variable definitions.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable entries with identifiers and descriptions for the tabular file collections, or state that the release ships no column-level data dictionary.

semantic_insights: The DOI prefix 10.18130 is University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), which matches the recorded publisher https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/ and the citation's repository name; format and registrar are both plausible and mutually consistent.

The NIH grant number 1OT2OD032742-01 parses correctly as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, and is the known Bridge2AI Other Transaction award; the secondary award 5U54HG012513-02 in the funder notes also parses as a valid NIH U54 to NHGRI.

The non-human-subjects claim is internally coherent across four independent blocks: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false, is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, sensitive_elements_present is false, and direct_collection.is_direct is false with cell-line provenance given. Nothing in the record contradicts the determination.

The deidentification statement is semantically appropriate for the data type. Naming HIPAA Safe Harbor or expert determination would be wrong for commercially sourced immortalized cell lines; the record instead gives the basis, that the data are non-clinical tissue-culture data that cannot be matched with current knowledge to a human subject, which is the correct claim for this material.

The licence chain is consistent in three places: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license and license_and_use_terms, the enum data_use_permission no_commercial_use, and a prohibited_uses entry whose stated reason is exactly the non-commercial clause plus the preprint's separate-negotiation requirement.

The representation-bias claim and the sampling strategy carry the same underlying statement: known_biases records representation_bias for de-identified cell lines not representing population-wide biological variation, and sampling_strategies sets is_representative false with that identical reason in why_not_representative.

Temporal ordering is coherent and its one oddity is disclosed. created_on 2025-02-27 precedes issued 2026-06-17, which precedes last_updated_on 2026-07-15, and the later date is explained by the three immunofluorescence archives being published Jul 15 2026 after the Jun 17 2026 release. source_caveats flags that the deposit date is reused verbatim from earlier releases and that the release page's description block carries a 2025-06-30 date.

Creator identifiers are well formed: 36 of 47 creators carry valid ORCID CURIEs, and the remaining 11 carry fragment identifiers minted on the record's own DOI rather than fabricated ORCIDs, which is the correct handling for people whose ORCID the sources do not give.

source_caveats does real epistemic work rather than hedging. It names the tier of each source, states which project-level counts were deliberately not asserted as release-level totals, and separates facts about superseded releases into related_datasets. That discipline is why the instance-count gap in Element 5 is an honest absence rather than an omission.

The related_datasets block distinguishes the U2OS multimodal cell map published in Nature from this dataset, typing it as references rather than absorbing its identifiers into this record's own distribution slots.

correctness_validations.doi_prefix_plausibility: plausible (10.18130 = University of Virginia Dataverse / LibraData, matches recorded publisher)
correctness_validations.orcid_format: valid (36 ORCID CURIEs well formed; 11 creators carry DOI-fragment ids rather than fabricated ORCIDs)
correctness_validations.url_validity: one_invalid (distribution_formats.access_urls is a truncated API base with no datafile id; all other URLs are well formed and plausible)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Format matches 10.XXXX/... and the 10.18130 prefix is University of Virginia Dataverse, consistent with the recorded publisher and citation. Identifier is expressed as a CURIE rather than a resolver URL.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta); description of roughly 1,500 characters naming each modality and cell line
sub_elements.quality_note: The description enumerates which modality covers which cell line and treatment condition and states the overarching objective, well beyond the 200-character threshold and specific enough to tell this release apart from its predecessors.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 30 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9, subcellular imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Well past the five-keyword threshold and spanning assay, cell line, perturbation agent, disease context and program, with abbreviations and expansions both present for retrievability.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; nine subsets and ten file_collections with names, MD5 checksums and sizes
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page plus a genuine two-level resource hierarchy in which each subset names the file collection that distributes it. The page points at the project portal rather than the release page on Dataverse, which the DOI supplies instead.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of links to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX and DXWOS5, plus is_described_by, is_referenced_by and references entries
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete version lineage back through four prior Dataverse releases with typed relationships and per-release notes on what each contained.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spelling out the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 permissions and conditions; ip_restrictions naming the Regents of the University of California and the Board of Trustees of Stanford as copyright holders and the Data Access Committee
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy, copyright ownership split by data package, and the commercial-licensing route are all stated. Actionable for a would-be reuser deciding whether they need a negotiation.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated for the release.'
sub_elements.quality_note: A determinate negative finding attributed to the release metadata, which answers the sub-element's question for a non-clinical cell-line dataset. Thin: no confidentiality_level classification, and HIPAA and GDPR are not addressed even to say they do not apply.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/; notes: 'Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API'; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform link and explicit access instructions including the browser size limit and the API fallback. Scored 1 on the instructions and the resolvable publisher plus DOI, with the truncated API base flagged as a correctness issue since that URL alone resolves to nothing.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP; media_type: application/zip; ten file_collections each with compression: zip, an MD5 checksum, a stated size from 30.2 KB to 4.6 GB and a publication date
sub_elements.quality_note: Container format, MIME type, per-file checksums and sizes are all present, which supports integrity checking and download planning. The interior data formats are not stated, flagged separately under Element 3.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets with seven typed entries; external_resources naming cm4ai.org, the MassIVE Repository, Figshare, NDEx, the Cell Mapping Toolkit GitHub repository, FAIRSCAPE and IMP
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots are substantively populated, and the external repositories are matched to the specific data they hold rather than listed generically.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, publisher is a public Dataverse instance, licence permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, with share, adapt, attribution, non-commercial and ShareAlike terms each spelled out
sub_elements.quality_note: An identifiable standard licence with its permissions and obligations stated in full, plus the attribution and citation expectation. A reuser can determine what they may do without leaving the record.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP; media_type: application/zip; is_tabular: false; encoding absent
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the archive container is declared. ZIP is standard but says nothing about how to read the contents, and the interior formats for imaging, mass spectrometry and single-cell data are all unstated, as is character encoding. Not enough to support integration with other data.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; conforms_to prose describing FAIRSCAPE packaging; notes naming the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology and the ARK identifier scheme
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels, with an unusually careful attribution of where the RO-Crate claim comes from. The prose caveat that the June 2026 release does not itself restate the packaging format is flagged as a low-severity confidence mismatch with the structured enum.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.evidence: variables slot absent; instances carry data_substrate and data_topic CURIEs such as B2AI_SUBSTRATE:59 and B2AI_TOPIC:26
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable-level metadata and no data dictionary. The ontology CURIEs identify modality and substrate, not columns, so the tabular members of the release such as the SEC-MS elution profiles and the perturb-seq atlas have no documented fields.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four use_category entries with examples; prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making and patient care, quoted verbatim from the release, and commercial use with the licence and preprint basis given
sub_elements.quality_note: Both directions of guidance are present, and each prohibition carries a reason rather than a bare assertion. The clinical prohibition is quoted from the source, which makes it checkable.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Governance disjunct satisfied through E2 rather than E4: ip_restrictions states that 'a Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use'. That is a governance constraint that applies, asserted in an E2 field, so the determination is non-circular. The human-subjects disjunct is not satisfied: E1 description and keywords name only cell lines and E8 collection_mechanisms describe no participant recruitment. regulatory_restrictions is a record that no restriction applies and was not counted, per #1060.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries naming Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon with ORCIDs and institutional emails, and describing a Value-Sensitive Design methodology and an axiological repository; data_governance.access_review_process describing the Data Access Committee; data_governance.committee_contact with ORCID and email
sub_elements.quality_note: Named, contactable ethical review with a stated methodology, a distinct data governance contact, and a described access review process. Oversight is documented as a standing structure rather than a one-off approval, which is the right shape for a dataset with no participants. Formal DPIA and conflict-of-interest disclosure are absent.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance disjunct as sub-element 1: E2 ip_restrictions states an applicable Data Access Committee constraint. The dataset also derives from donor material, the KOLF2.1J line from a healthy male Northern European donor via HipSci, which is the donor-derived case this sub-element's rationale names.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; deidentification_details: 'CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; human_subject_research.notes recording De-identified Samples: Yes
sub_elements.quality_note: The basis for the deidentification status is stated rather than merely asserted, and it is the semantically correct claim for commercially sourced immortalized cell lines, where naming Safe Harbor or expert determination would be wrong. The record gives a source-level determination rather than an applied technique, which is what the material admits.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met and the governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element. E1 description and keywords name only MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J cell lines and their derivatives, with no participant, patient or clinical-research terms; E8 collection_mechanisms describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, confocal imaging and CRISPRi screens with no participant recruitment. The Data Access Committee is a governance structure, and per #1060 a governance structure is not a participant signal.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants exist whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring this 0 would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met, on the same E1 and E8 evidence as sub-element 3; the governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element. direct_collection.is_direct is false, recording that data were generated from commercially available cell lines rather than collected from individuals.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants were enrolled, so there is no consent process to document.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The upstream donor consent for the KOLF2.1J line sits with HipSci, not with this dataset's collection.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met, on the same E1 and E8 evidence as sub-elements 3 and 4; the governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants were enrolled, so there is no at-risk population and no compensation to document.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations with identification by cell type and treatment condition and a distribution field giving modality coverage per condition; nine subsets each with is_subpopulation: true
sub_elements.quality_note: The distribution field does the work that matters: it states which modality covers which condition, so a user can tell that AP-MS covers treated MDA-MB-468 only while SEC-MS spans all seven cell states. Structured subset flags back the prose.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances lists four instance_type entries with no counts; total_file_count: 10; subsets carry is_data_split: false; source_caveats states 'the June 2026 release page does not state how many targets this release actually covers'
sub_elements.quality_note: No counts of images, cells, proteins, guides or targets at any level. Only a file count and per-archive sizes. The split flags are present but the sub-element's substance, how much data there is, is unanswered. The omission is honest and traced to the source, which the record says explicitly, but it leaves the question unanswered.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false; variables slot absent
sub_elements.quality_note: The tabular flag is present and correct for a release dominated by images and mass-spectrometry output, but no variable or column descriptions are given for the members that are tabular, notably the perturb-seq cell atlas and the SEC-MS elution profiles.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances with data_topic CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:15, :26 and :34 and data_substrate CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, :58, :59 and :64, plus instance_type descriptions and an imaging note giving the four stain channels
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are bound to ontology identifiers rather than free text, and the disease contexts of cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders are carried in the description and purposes. The immunofluorescence channel assignment is specific enough to interpret the images.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies with is_sample: true, is_random: false, is_representative: false, why_not_representative, strategies, source_data and a note distinguishing the project's stated 100-plus-100 target objective from what this release covers; known_limitations recording incomplete overlap between the protein sets interrogated by each modality
sub_elements.quality_note: Sampling is documented thoroughly and its non-representativeness is stated with a reason. The note separating a May 2024 project objective from this release's unstated coverage is exactly the kind of caveat the sub-element is for. anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: version: "2.0"; status: Beta
sub_elements.quality_note: An explicit version with a maturity status. Flagged separately as a content-accuracy issue that two earlier releases are recorded at Version 2.1, so the numbering does not increase monotonically across the chain.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available naming the May 2024, March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, 2.1) and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, 2.1) releases; latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Each prior version is reachable by its own DOI in the same Dataverse collection, and the latest version is named. A user can retrieve any earlier release directly.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.evidence: errata absent; updates.update_details states only the forward schedule, 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026'
sub_elements.quality_note: No errata and no change log. What did change is recoverable only indirectly from related_datasets notes, for instance that the October 2025 release 'did not include AP-MS data', but that is a description of the predecessor rather than a stated change record for this release.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: Quarterly; update_details giving the November 2026 project end date; retention_limit describing long-term preservation in the UVA Dataverse on committed institutional funds
sub_elements.quality_note: A stated cadence with an end date, plus a preservation commitment beyond it. Both the maintenance horizon and what happens afterwards are answerable.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources with seven entries naming source type and access location including the MassIVE Repository and Figshare; data_collectors naming the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and the Krogan laboratory at UCSF and the four producing institutions; source_caveats declaring the source tiering used
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is documented in both directions: upstream to the repositories holding the raw acquisitions, and laterally to the laboratories that generated each modality. was_derived_from and release_notes are absent but raw_data_sources carries the substance.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes with four responses, plus addressing_gaps with two responses on the black-box problem in genotype-phenotype learning
sub_elements.quality_note: The rationale is stated at both the scientific and the programmatic level, and addressing_gaps names the specific deficiency the dataset targets rather than restating the purpose.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks with five responses covering hierarchical cell map construction as directed acyclic graphs, self-supervised multimodal embedding, multi-resolution community detection, visible neural networks and genetic variant interpretation
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete computational tasks with named methods, not generic aims. A machine-learning user can tell what the data are shaped for.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders with grantor: National Institutes of Health and notes naming NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia
sub_elements.quality_note: The primary funder is structured and secondary support is named with its source attributed to the preprint rather than to the release page.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grants.grant_number: 1OT2OD032742-01
sub_elements.quality_note: Parses correctly against the NIH pattern as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, and matches the known Bridge2AI Other Transaction award. The secondary 5U54HG012513-02 in the notes also parses as a valid NIH U54 to NHGRI.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators with 47 entries carrying affiliations, 36 valid ORCID CURIEs, ROR identifiers for the University of Virginia, and a principal_investigator block for Trey Ideker with ORCID and email; maintainers naming four contacts with roles and emails
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is thorough and disambiguated. Where the sources give only surname and initial the record says so in a note and gives the full name from the preprint, rather than silently expanding or inventing. Creators without a known ORCID carry fragment ids on the record's own DOI instead of fabricated ones.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) and the datasets-shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms with four entries including the four immunofluorescence channels (DAPI for nuclei, calreticulin for endoplasmic reticulum, tubulin for microtubules, antibody against the protein of interest) and the CRISPRi library design at six guide RNAs per gene in inducible dCas9 lines read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit
sub_elements.quality_note: Settings are given at a level a lab could act on: stain targets by channel, guide density, induction system and sequencing kit.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods with three entries each carrying was_directly_observed: true, describing AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex mapping, Human Protein Atlas antibodies with robotic fixation and permeabilization, and single-cell CRISPRi screens; raw_data_sources naming MassIVE and Figshare

E8's own fields were not used as the signal.

The MuSIC pipeline in notes describes how the computed cell maps are built, but the record itself states those maps are not in this release, so it does not account for how the distributed processed files were derived.

sub_elements.evidence: external_resources naming the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io under the MIT License, IMP at http://integrativemodeling.org, NDEx with Cytoscape, HiView and the ndex2 Python library; notes describing the MuSIC pipeline components

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure

sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations with four typed entries: scope_limitation for the absent computed cell maps with a scope_impact field, coverage_limitation for incompletely overlapping protein sets across modalities, methodological_limitation on the domain expertise required, and coverage_limitation for the embargoed perturb-seq subsets
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, specific and consequential, and the scope_impact field states what the release is therefore suitable for. The embargo limitation is corroborated in raw_data_sources and third_party_sharing.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases with bias_type: representation_bias and the description that the data derive from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants seen in the population at large

Only one bias is recorded and future_use_impacts is absent, so anticipated downstream social impacts are not addressed.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies slot absent; no outlier, batch-effect, failed-run or quality-control discussion anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: The known_limitations entries are scope and coverage constraints rather than data quality findings. For a release combining imaging, mass spectrometry and single-cell sequencing, no quality-control outcome, failed-sample count or batch consideration is recorded.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements with sensitive_elements_present: false and sensitivity_details recording Human Subjects: No, De-identified Samples: Yes and FDA Regulated: No, with the basis that the data are non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and cannot be matched with current knowledge to a human subject
sub_elements.quality_note: A determinate finding with its reasoning, not an empty field. It is consistent with human_subject_research and is_deidentified, so a user gets a coherent answer on sensitivity across three blocks. content_warnings is absent, which is appropriate here.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews with two entries naming Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon with ORCIDs and emails, describing a Value-Sensitive Design methodology and an axiological repository; data_governance.notes describing the Ethics team's work on licensing, dissemination and Data Access supervision and the CM4AI Life Cycle governance framework
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical review is documented as named, contactable people with a stated methodology and an ongoing governance framework. Conflicts of interest are not disclosed, which is the one gap in an otherwise strong sub-element.

sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/; external_resources describing the portal as providing 'project overview, data releases, tools, product documentation, publications, and learning materials', plus https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/ and the FAIRSCAPE tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io
sub_elements.quality_note: A project portal explicitly offering learning materials, plus two separate technical documentation sites with tutorials. More than a bare landing page.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets with seven entries using is_new_version_of (four prior Dataverse releases), is_described_by (the CM4AI preprint), is_referenced_by (the perturbation atlas preprint) and references (the Nature U2OS cell map paper, with its NDEx uuid, MassIVE identifier MSV000097168 and ProteomeXchange identifier PXD052362)
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types are used precisely and the distinction between this dataset and the related-but-distinct U2OS cell map is maintained, with that dataset's identifiers kept inside its related_datasets note rather than absorbed into this record's own distribution slots.

strengths: Provenance discipline is the standout quality of this record. source_caveats declares the source tier used for each class of value, states which project-level counts were deliberately not asserted as release-level totals, and routes facts about superseded releases into related_datasets rather than into this record's own slots.

Attribution is thorough and honest: 47 creators with affiliations, 36 valid ORCID CURIEs, ROR identifiers for institutions, and DOI-fragment identifiers rather than fabricated ORCIDs for the 11 people whose ORCID the sources do not give, with full names recovered from the preprint recorded as notes.

The version lineage is complete and navigable. Four prior releases are linked by DOI with typed is_new_version_of relationships and per-release notes on what each contained, and version_access gives a direct retrieval route for each.

Collection and acquisition are documented at replication-level detail, including the four immunofluorescence stain channels and their targets, the CRISPRi library at six guide RNAs per gene in inducible dCas9 lines, the 10x Genomics 3'HT readout, and the rationale for using AP-MS and SEC-MS as orthogonal approaches.

The non-human-subjects determination is coherent across four independent blocks and semantically correct for the material. The record explains why the cell-line data are considered de-identified rather than asserting an inapplicable technique such as HIPAA Safe Harbor.

Licensing and use guidance form a consistent chain: the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms are spelled out, the data_use_permission enum matches, and both prohibited uses carry reasons, with the clinical prohibition quoted verbatim from the release so it is checkable.
weaknesses: No instance counts anywhere. The record reports four instance types, ten files and per-archive sizes, but no count of images, cells, proteins, guide RNAs or targeted genes, so the scale of the release cannot be determined from the metadata.

Only the ZIP container is declared as a format. The interior formats for imaging, mass spectrometry and single-cell data are unstated and no character encoding is given, which blocks the interoperability the licence otherwise permits.

Five file collections are typed processed_data while every processing field is empty. preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent, and the MuSIC pipeline in notes produces the cell maps the record says are not in this release.
No variable-level metadata or data dictionary, so the tabular members of the release, notably the SEC-MS elution profiles and the perturb-seq cell atlas, have no documented fields.

No data quality or anomaly documentation. The anomalies slot is empty and no quality-control outcome, failed-sample count or batch consideration is recorded for a release spanning three instrument platforms.
The only access URL is a truncated Dataverse API base with no datafile identifier, so no file in the release is individually addressable from this record despite each carrying an MD5 checksum.

Version numbering across the release chain is not monotonic. This June 2026 release is version 2.0 while two earlier releases are recorded at 2.1, and unlike the other date anomalies this one is not flagged in source_caveats.
The software_and_tools slot is empty while seven tools sit in external_resources and free-text notes, none of them with a version pin.
Conflicts of interest are not disclosed in ethical_reviews, and no formal data protection impact assessment is recorded alongside the Data Access Committee.
recommendations: Report release-level counts for each modality, or state per modality that the release page gives none. The record already establishes that discipline for target counts in sampling_strategies.notes and should extend it to images, cells and proteins.
Declare the interior data format and encoding for each file collection alongside the existing ZIP container and MD5 checksum, so a reuser knows what will read the contents.

Document the processing that produced the five processed_data archives, separately from the MuSIC pipeline that builds the excluded cell maps, or record explicitly that the release page does not describe it.
Append the Dataverse datafile identifiers to the access URL, or give each file_collection its own resolvable URL, so the checksums have addressable files to verify.
Add variables entries with identifiers and descriptions for the tabular members of the release, at minimum the perturb-seq cell atlas and the SEC-MS elution profiles.
Add a source_caveats note on the non-monotonic version numbering across the Dataverse collection, so a user comparing 2.0 against the earlier 2.1 releases is not misled about ordering.
Move the tool references into software_and_tools with repository URLs and, where the sources state them, version pins, keeping external_resources for the portals and repositories.
State whether the perturb-seq embargo applies to the external repository deposits only, given that both perturb-seq archives are distributed in this release with checksums and publication dates.
Record conflict-of-interest disclosures alongside the named ethical review contacts, and note whether a data protection impact assessment was undertaken or judged unnecessary.
